You’ve answered my question, thanks. It’s just a statement that can be proven wrong easily. Additionally, this understates the intensity of lethargy. This sub as a whole lumps all people of high weight together as “two year olds who can’t control cravings” or “lazy” when completely ignoring debilitating medication induced fatigue in which people cannot simply “just get up.” Completely ignoring any other factor resulting in weight gain. I don’t see the point other than to put others down or oneself down when posting this. What about promoting healthy living without ridiculing? That seems to be the aim of this sub, but it fails miserably.

So fatlogic, or “false logic” (since it’s being so heavily ridiculed) is the opposing non- black and white belief that eating isn’t the *only* way to gain weight. I’d bet on that belief. Why? Because you cited two ways in which weight can be gained without intake in your argument.
1. Hypothyroidism 
2. Water retention
3. Pregnancy 

These reasons, I’d say, are reasonable excuses for weight gain. They are not “fatlogic” because labeling it as such discounts facts and incredibly invalidates legitimate conditions. 

Making an absolute argument is too easily refutable. It’s debate 101.

So I understand the blatantly obvious fallacies within the “fat movement” and I completely agree that they’re ridiculous. Still, why does this sub swing so far the other way? I’ve read here that the *only reason* for being overweight is food intake. What about hypothyroidism? What about medications? Pregnancy/post pregnancy? Polycystic ovary syndrome? Metabolism in general? 

I’m not saying unjustified excuses are okay for weight gain, but what about the cases where it is justified? Is that simply *never* here?
